es: Distinguir en una discusión familiar las frases que acusan, las que describen hechos y los mensajes en primera persona, y encontrar la queja de fondo.

teaching.en: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.
teaching.es: Siempre me ignoras en las cenas familiares y, cada vez que saco un problema, simplemente le quitas importancia a mis preocupaciones.
teaching.explanationEs: Acusación: always y simply brush off juzgan a la persona en lugar de contar un hecho.
segments: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I
bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.
teaching.audioText: You always ignore me at family dinners, and whenever I bring up a problem you simply brush off my worries.

teaching.en: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the sink was full of dishes again when I got home.
teaching.es: Una descripción neutral solo cuenta lo que cualquiera podría ver: el fregadero estaba otra vez lleno de platos cuando llegué a casa.
teaching.explanationEs: Descripción neutral: hechos comprobables, sin juicio ni emoción.
segments: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the
sink was full of dishes again when I got home.
teaching.audioText: A neutral description only states what anyone could see: the sink was full of dishes again when I got home.

teaching.en: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.
teaching.es: Me siento frustrado cuando los planes cambian a última hora, porque entonces no puedo organizar bien mi semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Mensaje en primera persona: I feel + emoción + when + situación + because + consecuencia.
segments: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last
minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.
teaching.audioText: I feel frustrated when plans change at the last minute, because then I cannot organise my week properly.

teaching.en: You always blame me for everything, and that sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.
teaching.es: Siempre me echas la culpa de todo, y esa acusación tan generalizada hace imposible cualquier conversación tranquila.
teaching.explanationEs: Always y everything exageran: una acusación cierra la conversación aunque tenga algo de verdad.
segments: You always blame me for everything, and that
sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.
teaching.audioText: You always blame me for everything, and that sweeping accusation makes any calm conversation impossible.

teaching.en: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.
teaching.es: Me siento disgustado siempre que nadie me pide mi opinión, aunque es difícil decirlo sin sonar amargado.
teaching.explanationEs: Whenever = cada vez que; el mensaje nombra la emoción y el momento exacto en que aparece.
segments: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although
it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.
teaching.audioText: I feel upset whenever nobody asks for my opinion, although it is hard to say so without sounding bitter.

teaching.en: Behind this argument there is a real grievance: I feel ignored, and my resentment has been growing for months.
teaching.es: Detrás de esta discusión hay una queja de fondo: me siento ignorado, y mi resentimiento lleva meses creciendo.
teaching.explanationEs: La queja de fondo es lo que siente quien habla, no el reproche que dice en voz alta.
segments: Behind this argument there is a real grievance: I feel
ignored, and my resentment has been growing for months.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estas frases acusa a la otra persona en vez de describir un hecho?

choices.text: The phone rang twice during the whole dinner.
You never bother to ask how my day went.
I feel left out when dinner starts without me.

feedback.es: «You never bother…» generaliza con never y juzga a la persona: es una acusación.

hint.es: La acusación habla de lo que la otra persona «siempre» o «nunca» hace.

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada vez que intento sacar el tema del dinero, me quitas importancia.»

feedback.es: Bring up es el phrasal verb para sacar un tema en una conversación; raise no lleva up.

hint.es: Es el verbo que forma «___ up» con el significado de sacar un tema.

origin.text: Leo knows that something is wrong at home. Every time he tries to ___ up the subject of money, his father changes the subject.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me siento frustrado cuando cancelas a última hora.»

answer.text: I feel frustrated when you cancel at the last minute

feedback.es: El mensaje en primera persona sigue el orden emoción, when y situación.

hint.es: Empieza con I feel y la emoción va antes de when.

prompt.es: Escucha el relato del pódcast y elige cuál era la queja de fondo de la oyente.

choices.text: She was angry because her brother shouted back at her at the dinner table.
She felt hurt because her brother talked only about his own job.
Her news seemed to matter less to her brother than his phone.

feedback.es: La oyente dice que lo que dolía era sentir que su noticia no importaba; el teléfono y los gritos son solo el detonante.

origin.audio: On a podcast about family life, a listener describes a dinner that went badly. She says her brother kept checking his phone while she talked about her new job. She told him, You always ignore me, and he shouted back that she always blamed him for everything. Looking back, she realises that the phone was not the real problem. What hurt was the feeling that her news did not matter, and that resentment had been growing for months.

prompt.es: Con el mismo relato, elige qué respondió el hermano cuando ella le acusó.

choices.text: He said that she was always blaming him for everything.
He said that she never listened when he spoke to her.
He promised to ask about her new job after dinner.

feedback.es: El hermano devuelve la acusación: «she always blamed him for everything»; no dice que ella nunca escucha ni promete nada.

origin.audio: On a podcast about family life, a listener describes a dinner that went badly. She says her brother kept checking his phone while she talked about her new job. She told him, You always ignore me, and he shouted back that she always blamed him for everything. Looking back, she realises that the phone was not the real problem. What hurt was the feeling that her news did not matter, and that resentment had been growing for months.

prompt.es: Completa: «Siempre que pone música de madrugada, Mia se siente cansada.»

feedback.es: Whenever significa «siempre que» y une la emoción con el momento en que aparece.

origin.text: Mia does not mind the music itself. ___ her flatmate plays it after midnight, she feels tired at work the next day.

prompt.es: Escucha a Sara y elige qué actitud adopta ante su padre.

choices.text: She blames him for making every decision without asking her.
She asks firmly to be included, without accusing him of anything.
She hopes he will change the plans because she dislikes the hotel.

feedback.es: Sara nombra su emoción, reconoce que no hubo mala intención y pide participar: firme, sin acusar ni reprochar.

origin.audio: Sara put down her glass and looked at her father. I feel upset every time nobody asks for my opinion, she said quietly. Last week you chose the holiday dates, and on Sunday you paid for the hotel. I know you did not mean anything by it, Dad, but I would like to be part of these decisions. Her father said nothing for a moment. Then he nodded and took out the calendar.

prompt.es: Con la misma escena, elige para qué dice Sara «I know you did not mean anything by it».

choices.text: To soften her complaint so that he will not take it seriously.
To suggest that the holiday dates were a serious mistake.
To separate her feeling from any judgement about his intentions.

feedback.es: Esa frase evita que el mensaje suene a acusación: describe lo que ella siente, no lo que él pretendía; no suaviza la petición, que sigue en pie.

origin.audio: Sara put down her glass and looked at her father. I feel upset every time nobody asks for my opinion, she said quietly. Last week you chose the holiday dates, and on Sunday you paid for the hotel. I know you did not mean anything by it, Dad, but I would like to be part of these decisions. Her father said nothing for a moment. Then he nodded and took out the calendar.

prompt.es: Completa: «Es una descripción neutral: cuenta lo que pasó y no juzga a nadie.»

feedback.es: Una descripción neutral se limita a hechos comprobables; no añade emoción ni reproche.

origin.text: The report says that the living room was empty at noon and that the window was open. That is a ___ description: it states what happened and judges nobody.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Me siento disgustado siempre que cambian mis planes sin avisar.»

answer.text: I feel upset whenever my plans change without warning

feedback.es: Whenever sitúa el momento de la emoción justo después del mensaje I feel + emoción.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Mia y elige qué pretende con él.

choices.text: To let him know about the problem without attacking him.
To make him feel guilty by listing the exact times of the noise.
To warn him that she would complain to the landlord.

feedback.es: El mensaje solo describe hechos; Mia espera que el vecino saque la conclusión sin sentirse acusado.

origin.audio: Mia sent her neighbour a text that said: The music was still playing at two in the morning, and my window was open. She did not add a complaint or a request. Later she admitted that she hoped he would understand the message without being told what to do.

prompt.es: Lee el mensaje de Leo y elige qué queja de fondo esconden sus acusaciones.

choices.text: Leo is annoyed mainly because his sister leaves her things everywhere.
Leo feels that he carries the household work alone.
Leo believes that his sister does it on purpose to upset him.

feedback.es: Las cosas por medio son solo el detonante: tras «never» y «always» Leo dice que es el único a quien le importa la casa, y se siente solo con las tareas.

origin.text: Leo's message to his sister: You never wash up, and you always leave your things everywhere. I am tired of being the only one who cares about this flat.

prompt.es: Completa: «En realidad, la queja de fondo es que Tom siente que nadie nota su ayuda.»

feedback.es: La grievance es la queja de fondo: lo que realmente molesta bajo el reproche.

origin.text: Everyone thinks the argument is about the dishes. In fact, the real ___ is that Tom feels nobody notices his help.
